newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom to lift stake in Cook Is. Telecom.
newsitem.headline: Telecom to lift stake in Cook Is. Telecom.

text.p: WELLINGTON, July 2 - Telecom Corp of New Zealand is to lift its interest in Telecom Cook Islands to 60 percent control through a complex deal announced on Wednesday, the New Zealand Press Association reported.

Telecom NZ, which currently holds 40 percent of the government-owned company, has agreed to pay the Cook Islands government NZ$3 million for a further 20 percent, giving it "effective management control", a joint statement by Cook Islands Minister of Telecommunication Vaine Tairea and Associate Minister of State Owned Enterprises Tom Marsters said.

"Although TCNZ (Telecom NZ) will have majority representation on the board of Telecom Cook Islands, some matters which are particularly sensitive or important to the Cook Islands will require the approval of all directors and consent of cabinet if they are to be altered," said Tairea.

Among the changes requiring cabinet approval would be any move to increase tariffs above the rate of inflation or change the practice of charging uniform local, national and international tariffs for the whole of the Cook Islands.
Tairea welcomed the deal saying that the revenue derived from the investment would benefit all Cook Islanders.

"There has been some criticism in New Zealand of the size of Telecom's profits but I do not think that anyone in New Zealand would want to go back to the old days. Toll prices there fell with privatisation and the service provided to customers undoubtedly improved."

The sale of the stake in the phone company is part of a privatisation programme being pursued by the Cook Islands government. Telecom Cook Islands has annual revenue of around $12 million, over 5000 lines and seven satellite earth stations.
